The client forwards it unchanged and uploads or downloads nothing.

Available in cPanel 138 and later; requires the selected account's backup feature and is unavailable to demo/shared accounts. This starts a destructive in-place restore, with a six-hour cap. Returning operationId is submission rather than completion; poll operationStatus and inspect errors and warnings. No automatic retry or rollback is added by the client.

Omitting clean uses a merge: archive files overwrite counterparts while newer files are retained. Pass true to send clean=1, select a snapshot and remove files added since backup; false sends clean=0 for merge. This switch governs website files only. The nullable boolean argument preserves omitted defaults and explicit false, and never sends the unsafe string false.

Omitting restoreDatabases restores archive databases by default. Pass false to send restore_databases=0 and leave every database untouched; true sends 1. The string false is unsafe upstream because Perl treats it as true, so the typed argument is a nullable boolean. Restored databases are reset to their backed-up state, dropping later objects. The server documents a rollback snapshot for a failed database restore; the client does not promise whole-site atomicity.

database is repeatable and selects an archive subset; omit it while restoring databases to restore them all. id is not checked against domain, so use a backup listed for the intended domain. Paths and archive identities stay server-side.

clean.description: Whether to restore website files as a snapshot. Pass true to send integer 1, rebuild the document root from the archive and remove files added since the backup. Omit or pass null for the default merge, which keeps those files; false sends integer 0 for the same merge. This switch governs website files only. The pinned API warns that the string false is truthy in Perl and would select the destructive snapshot; the typed boolean argument sends only 0 or 1.

restore_databases.description: Whether to restore the archive databases. Omit or pass null for the server default 1. Pass false to send integer 0 and restore website files only, leaving every database untouched; true sends integer 1. Database restoration resets each database to its backed-up state and drops objects created since. The pinned API warns that the string false is truthy in Perl and would restore databases; the typed boolean argument sends only 0 or 1. To leave databases untouched, set this argument to false and omit database.
